messages:
omar: quick q — thinking about the proposed ingress policy for telemetry. do we fanout every incoming span to a per-customer namespace + global exporter, or do we route earlier and only forward to the per-customer pipeline when needed?
laura: my bias: route early using resource.attr (customer_id) and only fanout to per-customer exporters for customers with dedicated retention/rls. saves egress and exporter QPS.
jack: agreed but watch out for ordering and duplicate writes when we also have billing exports. if we route in collector, use the routing processor + attributes and ensure dedupe at the exporter side.
marta: cost angle — fanout multiplies storage + retention. for small customers we should store in a shared cold dataset and tag for RBAC. for enterprise customers we create per-customer datasets.
omar: RBAC question — dashboard & traceviewer should only see their spans. do we plan namespace-level ACLs or metadata filters in the app?
laura: namespace-level ACLs are cleaner. console can query a specific namespace id. fallback: query global index filtered by customer_id but that's slower.
jack: note on sampling: head-based sampling at ingress lets us throttle QPS without touching backend storage. we should combine with tail-based sampling for error/latency traces.
marta: +1. also we need quota enforcement before heavy processors. if a customer exceeds ingest quota, drop low-priority spans and emit a UsageAlert metric.
ingest-bot: ingest-stats @channel  — current 5m p50 ingest: 12.3k spans/s, top-customer spikes to 3.1k spans/s, some logs show backpressure on exporter pool.
sre-bot: alert: exporter-pool-saturation for region-us-east-1 triggered at 1812345660. recommended action: enable temporary throttling or fallback to shared-gateway.
omar: sketch of collector routing we were discussing:```yaml
processors:
  routing:
    table:
      - from_attribute: customer.id
        to_resource: true
        exporters: [per_customer_exporter, billing_exporter]
exporters:
  per_customer_exporter:
    endpoint: https://internal-sink.local/tenant/{customer.id}
  billing_exporter:
    endpoint: https://billing.local/otlp
service:
  pipelines:
    traces/tenant:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [routing, batch]
      exporters: [per_customer_exporter, billing_exporter]
```
laura: that looks close. make sure "to_resource: true" doesn't lose other resource attrs. also prefer templated exporter endpoints to be validated at config parse time.
jack: we also need a circuit-breaker on per_customer_exporter so a noisy tenant can't clog shared connections. connection pool + per-exporter concurrency limit.
marta: UX for rollout: feature-flag the per-customer fanout. start with a small canary of enterprise tenants and monitor write amplification, cost, and query latency in console.
omar: good. action items: 1) jack to prototype routing + exporter circuit-breaker (ETA 2d). 2) laura to draft namespace-ACL model for console (ETA EOD Tue). 3) marta to run cost projection for fanout vs shared retention (ETA Fri). 4) ops to add temporary throttling playbook for exporter saturation.
jack: noted. i'll post a short PR with a test config and a load test script.
laura: I'll mock the console queries for namespace ACLs and verify perf impact.
marta: I'll model 3 retention tiers and their cost multipliers.
omar: thanks — if anyone wants to join the canary sync ping me. :thumbsup:
